chvostek's sign.alt: A clinician taps just in front of the ear and watches the same side of the face for twitching.

trousseau's sign.alt: Upper-arm cuff with a straight forearm, flexed wrist, fingers held together and straight at the interphalangeal joints, and thumb drawn across the palm.

monofilament test.alt: A 10 gram filament bends against the sole while the patient closes their eyes.

kernig's sign.alt: The patient lies on their back with the hip flexed while the clinician extends the knee.

brudzinski's sign.alt: Gentle neck flexion is illustrated with the associated involuntary bending of hips and knees.

romberg test.alt: The patient stands with feet together and eyes closed while a clinician guards against falling.

pupil assessment.alt: A penlight approaches from the side; the examiner observes both pupils.

whispered voice test.alt: A clinician whispers from behind while the opposite ear is masked.

snellen chart.alt: One eye is covered while the patient reads a distant visual-acuity chart. This picture is not a calibrated chart.

amsler grid.alt: One eye is covered while the patient looks at the center dot. This illustration is not a calibrated screening grid.

confrontation visual fields.alt: Patient and examiner face each other and compare detection of a finger in the peripheral field.

allen test.alt: The examiner maintains radial pressure while releasing ulnar pressure and observing hand color.

capillary refill.alt: A nail bed is compressed until pale, then released to observe color return.

orthostatic vital signs.alt: Blood pressure and pulse are compared after supine rest and standing with assistance.

jugular venous distension.alt: A reclined patient is examined for neck venous pulsation relative to the sternal angle.

pulsus paradoxus.alt: A cuff and stethoscope compare pressures where sounds are intermittent versus continuous through breathing.

ankle-brachial index.alt: Arm and ankle systolic pressures are measured with cuffs and Doppler.

tactile fremitus.alt: The clinician compares vibration at matched locations on the back while the patient says ninety-nine.

egophony, bronchophony, whispered pector.alt: A stethoscope is used to compare transmitted spoken or whispered sounds over lung fields.

peak expiratory flow.alt: The patient seals their lips around a peak-flow meter and blows hard and fast.

rebound tenderness.alt: Two views contrast abdominal pressure with release, when rebound pain is elicited.

mcburney's point.alt: The right ASIS and navel are connected; McBurney point lies one-third of the way from the ASIS.

murphy's sign.alt: The clinician palpates under the right costal margin during inspiration.

rovsing's, psoas and obturator signs.alt: Three positioning examples show left-sided palpation, hip extension, and hip internal rotation.

cullen's and Grey Turner's signs.alt: Bruising around the navel is contrasted with bruising at a flank.

fluid wave and shifting dullness.alt: A midline hand dampens superficial transmission during the fluid-wave test; position changes shift fluid.

cva tenderness.alt: One hand covers the costovertebral angle while the other gently percusses its back.

post-void residual.alt: An ultrasound bladder scanner is placed over the lower abdomen after voiding.

phalen's test.alt: The backs of the hands touch with wrists flexed and fingers pointing down.

tinel's sign.alt: The median nerve at the palmar wrist is tapped; its finger distribution is highlighted.

straight leg raise.alt: A clinician lifts one leg by the heel while keeping the knee straight.

the 6 p's.alt: The clinician assesses the limb distal to a splint, including pain with passive stretch.

trendelenburg gait test.alt: The unsupported side of the pelvis drops when the standing hip abductors are weak.

nitrazine and fern tests.alt: A pH strip and a microscope view of dried branching crystals illustrate two fluid tests.

non-stress test.alt: External abdominal monitors connect to a fetal-heart-rate tracing.

apgar score.alt: A newborn assessment depicts color, pulse, reflex response, tone, and breathing.

ortolani and barlow maneuvers.alt: A training model illustrates flexed hips and knees and the directions of hip movement.

newborn reflexes.alt: Examples show rooting, palmar grasp, and the arm response of the Moro reflex.

ballard score.alt: Physical findings and neuromuscular observations are assessed together to estimate maturity.

pediatric vital sign assessment.alt: A child stays on a parent’s lap while breathing and other vital signs are assessed.

skin turgor.alt: Skin is lifted and released; quick recoil is compared with persistent tenting. Site and age affect interpretation.

mini-cog and mmse.alt: An interview and a clock-drawing example show the setting for cognitive screening.

cage questionnaire.alt: A nonjudgmental interview is paired with the four CAGE prompts.

aims.alt: The examiner observes face, tongue, limbs, and movement during structured tasks.

ciwa-ar.alt: A clinician interviews a patient and observes withdrawal symptoms using a structured score.

suicide risk assessment.alt: A clinician asks directly about suicide in a calm, attentive conversation.

mental status examination.alt: Interview and observation cover appearance, speech, mood, affect, thought, and cognition.

glasgow coma scale.alt: Eye, verbal, and motor responses are assessed and documented separately.

tonometry.alt: An applanation tonometer is positioned at a patient’s eye using a slit lamp.

homan's sign.alt: Historical dorsiflexion maneuver, explicitly labeled as not recommended for DVT screening.

braden scale.alt: A bedside assessment considers the six domains of pressure-injury risk.

rule of nines.alt: Adult front and back body surfaces are labeled with burn-area percentages.

babinski reflex.alt: The stroke travels up the outer sole, then across the ball toward the great toe; an inset shows an extensor response.

weber test.alt: Weber forehead placement and Rinne mastoid-to-ear comparison, with an interpretation table.

rinne test.alt: A tuning fork is placed on the mastoid, then beside the ear canal to compare bone and air conduction.

leopold's maneuvers.alt: Four panels show fundal, lateral, Pawlik, and pelvic grips; for the fourth, the examiner faces the feet.

fundal height.alt: A tape follows the abdominal curve from the pubic symphysis to the top of the uterus.
